items.q: How bad is China's housing collapse in numbers?
items.a: Roughly **~$18T** paper wealth erased — ~**20 years of gains** gone, prices back near **2006** levels after **35 consecutive months** of declines. Construction activity collapsed ~**22%**; 70 major cities were −3.5% YoY (May).

items.q: Why was housing more than "an investment" in China?
items.a: Chinese households parked ~**70%** of wealth in real estate (vs ~**25%** in the US) — the **wealth trap**. "It was your safety net, your social status, your college fund" under capital controls, weak deposits, and mistrusted stocks.

sections.title: How the boom became a reverse loop

items.q: What built the boom before it broke?
items.a: Privatized housing (late 1990s) → urbanization → cheap debt → local governments earning ~**40% of revenue from land sales** → pre-sold unfinished apartments → prices up ~**700% (2001–2017)**. Peak real estate + related ≈ **¼ of China's GDP**.

Beijing's **three red lines** (2020) cut leverage overnight. **Evergrande** (~$300B debt) and Country Garden failed; buyers paid mortgages on nonexistent units; confidence reverse-looped: stop buying → no pre-sale cash → more stalled projects → more fear.

Response includes a **7T yuan whitelist** to finish projects plus lower mortgage rates/down payments — yet analysts still expect another ~**4%** decline before possible **2027** stabilization. "If an entire government throwing trillions… can't call the bottom themselves, neither could you or I."

items.q: What structural forces keep pressure on prices?
items.a: **Aging**, fewer marriages, slower urbanization, and **tens of millions** of empty/unfinished units amplify the demand shortfall after the leverage shock.

sections.title: What it means for US investors

items.q: Is this a 2008-style bank contagion for the US?
items.a: **Not primarily** — low direct bank exposure + capital controls. Spillover hits via weaker China demand on **S&P multinationals**, steel/copper/cement (~50% world steel / ~60% cement at peak China construction), export dumping, and dollar strength.

items.q: Why isn't US housing the same trap?
items.a: US fundamentals differ: **undersupply** (~1.2M homes short), ~**25%** wealth in housing, and **30-year fixed** mortgages vs prepaid unfinished units + leveraged developers. Still: "**two Americas**" — Northeast/Midwest hot; Texas/Florida/Mountain West correcting (Austin −27% from peak).

items.q: What's the biggest takeaway if you never buy Chinese property?
items.a: "The biggest lesson… isn't just that real estate could fall, it's what happens when an entire country has too much of its wealth tied up in **one asset without any diversification**." Make sure your financial life never depends on a **single number going up**.
